The VTiFeCrZr and V35Ti35Fe15Cr10Zr5 high-entropy alloys with a weight of 30 gram were prepared by vacuum arc melting with high purity elements (the purity of every element was more than 99.9%) on a water-cooled copper mold in the argon atmosphere. Ingots were melted at least five times to ensure compositions homogeneous.
A sample was cut from the as-cast ingot and annealed at 1000 oC for 3 h in a vacuum furnace for microstructure comparison.

The VTiFeCrZr and V35Ti35Fe15Cr10Zr5 high-entropy alloys with a weight of 30 gram were prepared by vacuum arc melting with high purity elements (the purity of every element was more than 99.9%) on a water-cooled copper mold in the argon atmosphere. Ingots were melted at least five times to ensure compositions homogeneous.

around the two-theta 41.43 o and 42.20 o, there is a strongest peak (110), corresponding to two phases (BCC1 and BCC2), both with the BCC crystal structures, are identified in the alloy. The lattice parameters of these phases are 308 pm and 303 pm for V35Ti35Fe15Cr10Zr5 alloy in the as-cast state, respectively.
The DR and IR are BCC1 and BCC2, respectively.

The microstructure of the alloy was a typical solid solution dendritic crystal structure, mainly owing to the similar melting points and the infinite solid solution between principal elements of Ti and V.

At 700 oC, the yield strength of V35Ti35Fe15Cr10Zr5 HEA was about 500 MPa higher than that of candidate alloys.
The high hardness of V35Ti35Fe15Cr10Zr5 is mainly attributed to the solid-solution strengthening effect, which was observed in many other HEAs [27].

The slip of dislocation seemed to be confined to a certain slip plane and piled up at the phase boundaries, which makes the dislocation hard to slip or cross-slip. Hence, the yield strength increased.

at 800 oC (Fig.5 (b)), dislocations easy to move and distributed uniformly within the phase due to the effect of thermal activation, although they may slip along a certain direction initially. Therefore, the strength decreased.
